assertions.notes: Email links carry the capability token only in the URL fragment (#t=) and never in path or query (regex-checked on two captured confirmations). With the token, the Sites manage page (acme.menuza.test:3008/reserve/manage) loads unauthenticated (zero localStorage keys, no cookie) and shows first name B4En, Tuesday, November 17, 2026 6:00 PM, 2 guests, status Confirmed. GET /reservations/manage/calendar.ics with the token returns 200 text/calendar whose SUMMARY 'Reservation at Erdman - Brakus' and DTSTART 20261117T230000Z match the booking (18:00 America/New_York). FAILING clause: the manage link embedded in the captured email is http://localhost:3001/reserve/manage#t=... (the App origin) and 404s; the document GET http://localhost:3001/reserve/manage returned 404. This is the known local-dev defect recorded in library/user-testing.md (siteOrigin falls back to ENV.BASE_URL when the org has no custom domain); reported as the assertion outcome, not re-diagnosed.
assertions.limitations: The working manage page was reached at the correct Sites origin (http://acme.menuza.test:3008/reserve/manage#t=...) rather than by following the literal link in the email. The add-to-calendar link in the email is a Google Calendar template URL (external); per the contract's alternative I verified the .ics endpoint with the token instead. The manage page was opened in the assigned session (which had no Sites guest session) rather than a brand-new one; the unauthenticated state was verified directly (no localStorage keys, no session cookie).
